company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% versus the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the robotics and AI-driven machine vision space.

MillerKnoll beat FQ1 EPS at 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even excluding the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind — clean EPS of 42 cents still topped consensus. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed slightly while EPS guidance was left unchanged, and FQ2 EPS guidance midpoint of 46 cents is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st, replacing interim CFO Bob Fishman who will remain through the transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a routine leadership transition with no financial results or guidance update attached.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the Street's 13.85% estimate. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressures squeezing household budgets, and expects a relatively flat retail sales environment in fiscal 2027 without providing formal guidance. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The data represents a meaningful clinical readout in the highly competitive GLP-1 obesity drug space. This is a significant positive catalyst that puts VK2735 among the more potent weight loss profiles reported in the sector.

GLP-1 obesity drug space gets a positive data point from Viking's VK2735 showing 22% weight loss.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is the earnings note for Tuesday, September 22nd. No broad macro or Fed commentary in this morning's note — it's a pure earnings and company catalyst rundown, so let's get right into it.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat fiscal fourth quarter earnings at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but do not be fooled — this was a low-quality beat. Tariff refunds added 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO item added another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture is much weaker. Domestic comps came in at just plus 1.6% versus the Street expecting plus 3.1%, and operating expenses as a percentage of sales worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did note improving sales trends in the final eight weeks of the quarter, which is something, but the headline beat masks real underlying softness.

Cognex is acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly $500 million upfront plus about $106 million more. RealSense is projected to do $80 to $90 million in revenue, growing more than 50% year-over-year. This is a strategic move deeper into the robotics and AI vision space and reads as a bullish catalyst for Cognex.

MillerKnoll put up a solid beat on fiscal first quarter earnings — 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents. Importantly, even backing out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, clean earnings of 42 cents still beat. Sales missed at $923 million versus the $943 million consensus, but orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full year guidance was trimmed slightly on the revenue line, EPS guidance was left unchanged, and the fiscal second quarter midpoint is in line with consensus. Call it mixed with a slight lean positive.

THOR Industries missed fiscal fourth quarter earnings at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents. Gross margins dropped 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the Street's 13.85% estimate. Management's tone was cautious — citing interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation squeezing consumers during what should have been the critical selling season. They're not providing formal fiscal 2027 guidance yet, but expect flat retail. The one genuine bright spot is the North American towable RV order backlog, which surged roughly 75% year-over-year.

The biggest mover this morning is Viking Therapeutics. Shares are spiking in pre-market after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 obesity drug, showing 22% weight loss. That is a standout number in a crowded and competitive space, and it puts Viking squarely in the conversation alongside the category leaders.

Pentair named a new CFO — Bob Hau, effective November 1st — a routine transition with no financial impact.

Bottom line for today: the earnings slate is mixed. AutoZone's beat has quality concerns. THOR is a clean miss with a tough macro backdrop. MillerKnoll is modestly encouraging. Viking is the high-conviction bullish catalyst of the morning. Watch how the GLP-1 trade reacts across the sector and whether AutoZone's comp miss weighs on auto parts retail broadly.
